Ally Care Team (ACT) Supervisor (6811U), University Health Services #90061 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
For over 100 years, UHS has been providing health care and integrative services for a wide range of physical and mental health care needs to the Berkeley campus community. And we've spent a quarter-century of that time at the Tang Center, a fully accredited health care facility, UHS employs over 300 people, including primary and urgent care physicians, psychiatrists, consulting medical specialists, nurse practitioners, registered nurses, pharmacists, health educators, social workers, and other health administrative professionals. All our clinicians, counselors, and nurses are state-licensed and/or certified in their respective fields. In addition to our staff, Berkeley students participate in UHS peer, intern, and volunteer programs. Together, we provide services on a continuum from prevention through treatment.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
Under the direction of the Manager of Behavioral Health, the incumbent will provide direct supervision and clinical oversight of mobile crisis operations, performing a wide range of complex tasks with a high level of autonomy. Supervises licensed clinicians and training staff providing mobile crisis responses to the campus, including the University Village site. Supervises and evaluates the work of clinical and non-clinical team members, including staff student workers. Responsible for evaluating and ensuring the quality of Mobile Crisis services. Involves psychological evaluation, diagnosis, counseling, psychotherapy, and crisis intervention with individuals and groups across a broad spectrum of developmental and psychological concerns that interfere with effective academic and personal functioning. Develops psycho-educational programs. Also performs one or more of the following functions: Uses and interprets educational, vocational, and psychological tests; provides clinical supervision of professional graduate-level trainees. Must be licensed as a Psychologist, Social Worker, or Licensed Marriage and Family Counselor in California. Ensures provider adherence to professional standards, internal policies, and external regulations. Provides high-level consultation to staff, often regarding complex, high-risk issues. Participates in the development and maintenance of crisis services delivery policies and procedures, and offers relevant training for staff. Assists the Manager of Behavioral Health in the evaluation and improvement of clinical processes to ensure the quality of mobile crisis services delivery.
  
  
This position is a clinical-supervisory role. Approximately 50-60% of the work involves direct clinical care within an integrated behavioral health model spanning primary care, urgent care, and campus-based response. The remaining 40-50% includes clinical supervision of 4-6 Clinicians, workflow coordination, and cross-branch collaboration.
  
Care includes supporting immediate mental health needs across campus in collaboration with campus partners, including consultation and response support with UCPD, Residential Life, faculty and staff, Title IX, Path to Care, and other campus teams. The work can be time-sensitive and may not follow a predictable clinic schedule.
  
As a supervisor, you will coordinate clinician coverage across the Behavioral Health team and the Campus Response team, ensuring that daily staffing, field deployments, and consultation requests are managed effectively. You will provide direct consultations, and serve as a bridge between the clinical team and broader campus partners.
  
The day-to-day work is fast-paced and highly collaborative within campus and medical settings. Clinicians provide same-day behavioral health assessment, brief intervention, crisis support, and care coordination in close collaboration with medical providers. Warm handoffs, rapid transitions, and occasional session interruptions are core expectations. As supervisor, you will model this work while supporting your team in navigating it.
  
We recognize this is a unique role. We will provide training on the model, workflows, and coordination practices. If you bring strong clinical fundamentals, supervision experience, sound judgment, and interest in integrated campus-based work, we can support the learning curve.

Departmental Overview
  
  
University Health Services (UHS) is a comprehensive college health service providing fully accredited, primary medical care, counseling and psychological services, and innovative health promotion programs for students, faculty, and staff. UHS provides on-campus medical care and coordinates supplemental needs for off-campus care through a network of community specialists and hospitals. UHS manages the student health insurance and workers' compensation insurance programs.
  
  
UHS provides services to students Monday through Friday from 8:00AM to 6:00PM and on weekends. Approximately 65,000 visits occur annually including Primary Care, Urgent Care, Occupational Health, and Specialty Clinics. Services are designed to enable students to get the most from their educational experience, minimizing the impact of illness, injury and emotional distress on their academic careers. Medical care and wellness programs for faculty and staff are designed to meet their occupational health needs and minimize lost work time. These visits all generate ancillary encounters with the Radiology, Clinical Laboratory, Physical Therapy and Pharmacy departments. The Counseling and Psychological Services department sees an additional 15,000 visits per year.

A Patient Services Representative serves as the first point of contact for patients and clients, providing a welcoming and professional environment. The position manages patient registration, check-in and check-out processes, schedules appointments, verifies insurance information, and maintains accurate patient records. This role also coordinates communication between patients and healthcare providers, handles phone inquiries, and ensures efficient administrative operations. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and excellent customer service are essential to support a positive patient experience.

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

Position: **Human Resources Coordinator**  
Term: Full-time, hourly  
Pay: $30.00/hour + health insurance, paid time off, and other benefits  
Location: San Francisco, CA or Los Angeles, CA  
Reports To: Deputy Director, Human Resources  
Direct Reports: None

**ORGANIZATION DESCRIPTION**  
Urban Alchemy hires individuals who were once incarcerated and trains them to transform people and places through love and respect. We provide services that heal communities challenged by the intersection of extreme poverty, mental illness, addiction, and homelessness. When individuals are suffering in our public spaces, Urban Alchemy offers solutions. When a neighborhood, street, or intersection earns a reputation as a place to avoid, we turn it around. Urban Alchemy staff, known as Practitioners, create a peaceful and supportive presence, helping our communities rebuild a sense of pride one person at a time. Urban Alchemy is a nonprofit organization founded in 2018. We quickly grew from a small program in San Francisco to a thriving social enterprise with over 1,000 staff. We currently operate in California, Alabama, Colorado, Georgia, New Mexico, and Oregon. Over 95% of Urban Alchemy employees, including leadership, experienced incarceration and/or homelessness. For more information visit our website.

**POSITION SUMMARY**  
The Human Resources Coordinator plays a vital role in keeping our day-to-day HR operations running smoothly, accurately, and supportively. This position oversees core administrative workflows that touch every employee across Urban Alchemy: onboarding, I-9 compliance, background check reviews, employment verifications, wage garnishments, and child support withholding orders. Because these areas directly influence legal compliance and an employee's livelihood, the Coordinator ensures each process is completed thoroughly, accurately, and on schedule.

Success in this role relies on consistency, thoughtful organization, and dependable follow-through. We look for someone who manages their daily desk with structured care, keeping clear track of active requests, monitoring upcoming milestones, and seeing items through to completion.

Based in Urban Alchemy's San Francisco or Los Angeles offices and supporting all operational regions, the Coordinator works directly with Practitioners during the onboarding journey. Many of our team members are justice-impacted individuals who may be navigating digital platforms and online onboarding tools for the first time. This calls for genuine warmth, patience, and a helpful, welcoming approach. As one of the first touchpoints a Practitioner has with our HR team, the Coordinator sets an encouraging, positive tone for their experience with Urban Alchemy.

**POSITION DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

A Note on the Nature of This Work  
Even in a fast-paced, high-volume environment, the details matter. Timely compliance for garnishments and I-9s ensures our organization meets essential legal standards, while an accurate onboarding packet directly shapes a new hire's first paycheck and their first impression of our community.

The Coordinator manages their caseload with a clear, proactive approach: tracking open items, anticipating deadlines, and keeping communication open across teams. When questions or potential delays arise, they surface them early, document the process, and partner collaboratively to find solutions before timelines are impacted.

**Onboarding Administration**  

* Own the full onboarding workflow for all new hires across Urban Alchemy regions, from offer acceptance through completion of all required documentation
* Coordinate with new hire Practitioners to complete onboarding paperwork via Paycom, including assisting individuals who are new to email, smartphones, or digital platforms; this may include helping a new hire set up a personal email account from scratch so they can receive and complete their onboarding link
* Maintain onboarding accuracy and completion rates at a high standard; missing or incomplete documentation creates downstream compliance risk and payroll delays
* Communicate weekly with the training team to confirm which new hires have completed their onboarding documentation in Paycom and are cleared to attend the following week's New Employee Orientation (NEO), so trainers can prepare accordingly
* Communicate clearly and proactively with HR team members and Operations when onboarding issues arise
* Travel to other Urban Alchemy regions to support in-person onboarding when a new region is being established or when operationally required

**Pre-Employment Compliance: I-9 and Background Checks**  

* Manage I-9 form completion for all new hires in compliance with federal requirements, including timely completion, proper document review, and accurate recordkeeping
* Conduct regular audits of I-9 records to identify and remediate compliance gaps before they become violations
* Stay current on I-9 regulatory requirements and flag any changes that affect current processes
* Review background check results for all new hires, identify any disqualifying findings per Urban Alchemy policy, and escalate promptly so the appropriate HR leader can initiate the FCRA individualized assessment process
* Understand that background check review is not passive; the Coordinator is responsible for reading results carefully, recognizing what requires escalation, and moving quickly so the interactive process can begin without delay
* Maintain complete and accurate records of all background check outcomes and escalations

**Garnishment Processing**  

* Receive, review, and process all garnishment orders accurately and in compliance with applicable federal and state laws
* Process garnishment orders in Paycom using the garnishment feature, which applies the deduction directly to the employee's profile; the Coordinator is responsible for timely and accurate upload so deductions are applied correc

Hundred Health is a modern telehealth platform that helps people optimize their health through advanced diagnostics. **What You'll Do**

* **Asynchronous protocol reviews:** Review system-generated protocols against each member's biomarker results, current medications and health history. Confirm or refine recommendations, and add brief personalized notes.
* **Medication awareness:** Spot where a member's medications may affect their lab results or interact with recommended supplements, and flag it for our clinical team
* **Recommend next steps:** Flag when follow-up or more lab testing would be valuable
* **Asynchronous messaging:** Respond in writing to member questions about their protocol and results
* **Rx program triage:** Help triage messages and requests from members in our prescription programs, routing clinical concerns to the right provider and flagging anything urgent
* **Close the loop:** Share member feedback and clinical insights with our internal team to improve protocols, content and product

* Deep working knowledge of lab and biomarker interpretation (metabolic, hormonal, cardiovascular, inflammatory and nutrient markers)

* Clinical or operational triage experience strongly preferred: you know when something can wait and when it needs a provider now
* Strong foundation in nutrition and evidence-based supplementation
* Clear, warm written communication
* Comfortable with technology and virtual care platforms

Ardovia is an all-in-one platform for pool builders and construction companies, covering leads, proposals and pricing, scheduling, job costing, purchasing, and the field mobile app. Demand is growing fast, and we need someone to own getting new customers live and successful.
